    "title": "Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/linear",
    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-80421\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints\",\n  \"status\": \"In Review\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-02-12\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-02-20\",\n  \"creator\": \"Sofia Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Marcus Rivera\",\n  \"project\": \"Hosted API Stabilization\",\n  \"cycle\": \"2025-W07\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2025-03-14\",\n  \"release\": \"hosted-api-2025.03\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"medium\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"api\",\n    \"launch\",\n    \"hosted\",\n    \"chat\",\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"rerank\",\n    \"acceptance\"\n  ],\n  \"summary\": \"Define prioritized scope, explicit acceptance criteria, and a conservative rollout plan for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints with clear gating metrics and operational runbooks.\",\n  \"background\": \"Redwood needs a single coordinated PRD that sets a prioritized subset of hosted API features for the next public launch window. Multiple product docs exist focusing on surface design, but there is inconsistent acceptance criteria between teams which risks divergent rollout readiness and customer confusion. This ticket consolidates decisions, defines measurable acceptance gates, and produces a launch checklist that can be followed by PM, Eng, Design, and Support.\",\n  \"goals\": [\n    \"Agree on a minimum viable capability set for public hosted API launch across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank\",\n    \"Produce an acceptance matrix with pass/fail gating metrics for functional, performance, and security requirements\",\n    \"Define a staged rollout plan (canary -> regional scaling -> general availability) with rollback conditions\",\n    \"Deliver an actionable launch checklist and handoff artifacts for support, docs, and partner teams\"\n  ],\n  \"non_goals\": [\n    \"Shipping dedicated or private deployment bundles (separate project)\",\n    \"Complete SDK language parity for all non-core SDKs\\u2014we will ship core JS/Python first\",\n    \"Large scale model training or onboarding of new architectures\\u2014this is focused on serving and surface stability\"\n  ],\n  \"product_requirements\": [\n    \"Endpoint coverage: chat, completions, embeddings (single and batched), rerank (server-side) must be exposed via REST + OpenAPI spec\",\n    \"API contract stability: response schemas must be versioned and backward compatible unless a major version bump is announced\",\n    \"Authentication: OAuth2 and API keys supported; SSO/SAML enterprise flow documented and validated in private tests\",\n    \"Structured output: function/tool-calling primitives available on chat endpoints with schema validation hooks\",\n    \"Batching & latency knobs: server-side batching must be configurable per-route; default config must meet SLO targets\",\n    \"Quotas & rate limiting: tier-aware defaults + per-customer overrides; error responses must include retry-after headers where applicable\"\n  ],\n  \"endpoint_specific_requirements\": [\n    \"Chat: streaming (chunked) responses, SSE support in REST, conversation state token included for KV cache affinity\",\n    \"Completions: single-turn responses, max_tokens enforcement, temperature/top_p controls, stopping sequences honored\",\n    \"Embeddings: deterministic outputs for same model+input+params; support both single and up-to-8-batch endpoints; embedding dimensionality documented\",\n    \"Rerank: accept candidate lists up to configured max, return score per candidate and stable ranking semantics; provide opt-out for full-text features for privacy-conscious customers\"\n  ],\n  \"performance_slos\": [\n    \"99th percentile latency for completions (1k tokens) <= 300ms for cached/short sequences under hosted free-tier load profile\",\n    \"Median generation latency for chat (stream resume) <= 150ms per chunk for standard models\",\n    \"Embeddings throughput target: 500 qps per shard with p95 latency <= 70ms for single input\",\n    \"Availability SLO: 99.9% regional during GA for core endpoints (excludes scheduled maintenance)\"\n  ],\n  \"telemetry_and_observability\": [\n    \"Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics in Console\",\n    \"Tracing hooks for request lifecycle (ingress -> model -> response stream) with sampling at 10%\",\n    \"Failure classification: distinguish client error, quota, model OOMs, runtime backpressure, and network errors\",\n    \"Alerting: burn rate alerts for error spikes and latency regressions with documented on-call escalation path\"\n  ],\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"API: OpenAPI spec file committed and published; example requests + SDK snippets for JS/Python included\",\n    \"Compatibility: backward compatibility test suite green across 3 prior minor revisions for response schemas\",\n    \"Performance: load test for target customer profile executed and p95/p99 metrics within SLO budget\",\n    \"Security: threat model review completed and critical/major findings remediated; KMS integration tested end-to-end\",\n    \"Reliability: automated canary pipeline validates new model binary for 72h at canary traffic with zero severity incidents\",\n    \"Docs: Console docs and quickstarts published; migration guide for customers with earlier endpoint variants\",\n    \"Support readiness: runbook (incident + FAQ) authored and triaged with L2 and L3 on-call; training session held\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Phase 0 - Internal Staging: Burn-in with internal teams and partner beta customers for 2 weeks\",\n    \"Phase 1 - Canary (5% traffic): Route small percentage of production traffic; monitor canary-specific metrics and automated rollback windows\",\n    \"Phase 2 - Regional Expansion (50% region): Open to more customers in region, enable quotas and limits enforcement\",\n    \"Phase 3 - GA (100%): Full exposure worldwide with pricing and quota tiers; start marketing motion\"\n  ],\n  \"canary_metrics_and_gates\": [\n    \"Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline -> automatic rollback\",\n    \"Latency p95 regression > 30% vs baseline -> hold promotion and trigger perf triage\",\n    \"Client-facing correctness failures (schema mismatch, missing fields) > 0 in canary logs -> fail promotion\",\n    \"Cost burn rate > 150% of predicted budget for canary segment -> pause and investigate caching/batching settings\"\n  ],\n  \"launch_checklist\": [\n    \"Finalize API surface and freeze non-breaking changes\",\n    \"Sign-off from Security on pen-test and KMS integration\",\n    \"Ops runbooks published (on-call, escalation, rollback) and verified via tabletop exercise\",\n    \"Console dashboards for tokens/cost/latency per route are live and pre-populated with synthetic traffic\",\n    \"SDK release candidates (JS/Python) published with migration notes\",\n    \"Billing & quotas pipelines connected and validated end-to-end with test customer accounts\",\n    \"Support FAQ and primary triage playbook published in Knowledge Base\",\n    \"Multi-region deployment validated and health checks automated\"\n  ],\n  \"migration_and_deprecation_strategy\": [\n    \"Provide explicit deprecation timeline for legacy endpoint variants with automated translation layer for 6 months\",\n    \"Offer opt-in compatibility headers for customers who need strict legacy behaviour\",\n    \"Measure adoption and provide targeted outreach for top 50 customers before hard deprecation\"\n  ],\n  \"risks_and_mitigations\": [\n    \"Risk: Model OOMs at tail causing request failures -> Mitigation: reserve fallback model variant with lower memory profile and graceful degradation\",\n    \"Risk: Schema changes break downstream SDKs -> Mitigation: strict schema validation in CI + backwards compatibility test harness\",\n    \"Risk: Cost overruns from unbounded batching -> Mitigation: default per-route throttles + billing alerts\",\n    \"Risk: Entitlement or quota misconfig leads to customer impact -> Mitigation: staged rollout with quota enforcement and explicit billing tests\"\n  ],\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"Runtime team: batching and KV cache toggles must be available via route config\",\n    \"Console: dashboards and rollout controls implemented and tested\",\n    \"SDK: JS and Python clients with new API surface and streaming primitives\",\n    \"Security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration completion\",\n    \"Legal/Billing: pricing tiers agreed and billing pipeline tested\"\n  ],\n  \"stakeholders\": [\n    \"PM: Sofia Patel\",\n    \"Eng (Runtime): Priya Natarajan\",\n    \"Eng (API): Marcus Rivera\",\n    \"Design: Leo Martinez\",\n    \"Security: Hannah Kim\",\n    \"Support: Anika Shah\",\n    \"Sales: Daniel Ortiz\"\n  ],\n  \"open_decisions\": [\n    \"Final verb names for streaming endpoints (stream vs SSE vs chunked) \\u2014 decision needed by 2025-02-25\",\n    \"Default batching window (20ms vs 40ms) \\u2014 leaning 20ms but waiting perf test results\",\n    \"Embeddings batch size max: 8 or 16 \\u2014 impact analysis in progress\"\n  ],\n  \"links\": [\n    \"Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-api/acceptance-matrix\",\n    \"OpenAPI: https://api.redwood.ai/specs/hosted-api-2025-03.yaml\",\n    \"Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/design/hosted-api-console-rollout\",\n    \"Load tests: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/hosted-api-canary-2025-02\",\n    \"PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8153\"\n  ],\n  \"comments\": [\n    \"2025-02-13 Sofia Patel: Initial draft posted; asked runtime and API leads for input on batching knobs.\",\n    \"2025-02-15 Marcus Rivera: Added definitive API contract section and requested OpenAPI generation from API infra team.\",\n    \"2025-02-17 Priya Natarajan: Raised concern about default caching affinity for chat; proposed 'conversation_token' header to improve KV hit rate.\",\n    \"2025-02-18 Hannah Kim: Security review scheduled for 2025-02-21; noted KMS integration needs test fixture for key rotation\",\n    \"2025-02-20 Design sign-off: Leo Martinez reviewed console flows; requested explicit error states for streaming interruptions\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"summary\",\n    \"background\",\n    \"goals\",\n    \"non_goals\",\n \"open_decisions\",\n    \"links\",\n    \"comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_6f6a548d740249f6a1413a8ab778f270\"\n}",

document.title: Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-80421",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints",
  "status": "In Review",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-02-12",
  "updated_at": "2025-02-20",
  "creator": "Sofia Patel",
  "assignee": "Marcus Rivera",
  "project": "Hosted API Stabilization",
  "cycle": "2025-W07",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2025-03-14",
  "release": "hosted-api-2025.03",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "customer_impact": "medium",
  "labels": [
    "api",
    "launch",
    "hosted",
    "chat",
    "embeddings",
    "rerank",
    "acceptance"
  ],
  "summary": "Define prioritized scope, explicit acceptance criteria, and a conservative rollout plan for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints with clear gating metrics and operational runbooks.",
  "background": "Redwood needs a single coordinated PRD that sets a prioritized subset of hosted API features for the next public launch window. Multiple product docs exist focusing on surface design, but there is inconsistent acceptance criteria between teams which risks divergent rollout readiness and customer confusion. This ticket consolidates decisions, defines measurable acceptance gates, and produces a launch checklist that can be followed by PM, Eng, Design, and Support.",
  "goals": [
    "Agree on a minimum viable capability set for public hosted API launch across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank",
    "Produce an acceptance matrix with pass/fail gating metrics for functional, performance, and security requirements",
    "Define a staged rollout plan (canary -> regional scaling -> general availability) with rollback conditions",
    "Deliver an actionable launch checklist and handoff artifacts for support, docs, and partner teams"
  ],
  "non_goals": [
    "Shipping dedicated or private deployment bundles (separate project)",
    "Complete SDK language parity for all non-core SDKs\u2014we will ship core JS/Python first",
    "Large scale model training or onboarding of new architectures\u2014this is focused on serving and surface stability"
  ],
  "product_requirements": [
    "Endpoint coverage: chat, completions, embeddings (single and batched), rerank (server-side) must be exposed via REST + OpenAPI spec",
    "API contract stability: response schemas must be versioned and backward compatible unless a major version bump is announced",
    "Authentication: OAuth2 and API keys supported; SSO/SAML enterprise flow documented and validated in private tests",
    "Structured output: function/tool-calling primitives available on chat endpoints with schema validation hooks",
    "Batching & latency knobs: server-side batching must be configurable per-route; default config must meet SLO targets",
    "Quotas & rate limiting: tier-aware defaults + per-customer overrides; error responses must include retry-after headers where applicable"
  ],
  "endpoint_specific_requirements": [
    "Chat: streaming (chunked) responses, SSE support in REST, conversation state token included for KV cache affinity",
    "Completions: single-turn responses, max_tokens enforcement, temperature/top_p controls, stopping sequences honored",
    "Embeddings: deterministic outputs for same model+input+params; support both single and up-to-8-batch endpoints; embedding dimensionality documented",
    "Rerank: accept candidate lists up to configured max, return score per candidate and stable ranking semantics; provide opt-out for full-text features for privacy-conscious customers"
  ],
  "performance_slos": [
    "99th percentile latency for completions (1k tokens) <= 300ms for cached/short sequences under hosted free-tier load profile",
    "Median generation latency for chat (stream resume) <= 150ms per chunk for standard models",
    "Embeddings throughput target: 500 qps per shard with p95 latency <= 70ms for single input",
    "Availability SLO: 99.9% regional during GA for core endpoints (excludes scheduled maintenance)"
  ],
  "telemetry_and_observability": [
    "Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics in Console",
    "Tracing hooks for request lifecycle (ingress -> model -> response stream) with sampling at 10%",
    "Failure classification: distinguish client error, quota, model OOMs, runtime backpressure, and network errors",
    "Alerting: burn rate alerts for error spikes and latency regressions with documented on-call escalation path"
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "API: OpenAPI spec file committed and published; example requests + SDK snippets for JS/Python included",
    "Compatibility: backward compatibility test suite green across 3 prior minor revisions for response schemas",
    "Performance: load test for target customer profile executed and p95/p99 metrics within SLO budget",
    "Security: threat model review completed and critical/major findings remediated; KMS integration tested end-to-end",
    "Reliability: automated canary pipeline validates new model binary for 72h at canary traffic with zero severity incidents",
    "Docs: Console docs and quickstarts published; migration guide for customers with earlier endpoint variants",
    "Support readiness: runbook (incident + FAQ) authored and triaged with L2 and L3 on-call; training session held"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Phase 0 - Internal Staging: Burn-in with internal teams and partner beta customers for 2 weeks",
    "Phase 1 - Canary (5% traffic): Route small percentage of production traffic; monitor canary-specific metrics and automated rollback windows",
    "Phase 2 - Regional Expansion (50% region): Open to more customers in region, enable quotas and limits enforcement",
    "Phase 3 - GA (100%): Full exposure worldwide with pricing and quota tiers; start marketing motion"
  ],
  "canary_metrics_and_gates": [
    "Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline -> automatic rollback",
    "Latency p95 regression > 30% vs baseline -> hold promotion and trigger perf triage",
    "Client-facing correctness failures (schema mismatch, missing fields) > 0 in canary logs -> fail promotion",
    "Cost burn rate > 150% of predicted budget for canary segment -> pause and investigate caching/batching settings"
  ],
  "launch_checklist": [
    "Finalize API surface and freeze non-breaking changes",
    "Sign-off from Security on pen-test and KMS integration",
    "Ops runbooks published (on-call, escalation, rollback) and verified via tabletop exercise",
    "Console dashboards for tokens/cost/latency per route are live and pre-populated with synthetic traffic",
    "SDK release candidates (JS/Python) published with migration notes",
    "Billing & quotas pipelines connected and validated end-to-end with test customer accounts",
    "Support FAQ and primary triage playbook published in Knowledge Base",
    "Multi-region deployment validated and health checks automated"
  ],
  "migration_and_deprecation_strategy": [
    "Provide explicit deprecation timeline for legacy endpoint variants with automated translation layer for 6 months",
    "Offer opt-in compatibility headers for customers who need strict legacy behaviour",
    "Measure adoption and provide targeted outreach for top 50 customers before hard deprecation"
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigations": [
    "Risk: Model OOMs at tail causing request failures -> Mitigation: reserve fallback model variant with lower memory profile and graceful degradation",
    "Risk: Schema changes break downstream SDKs -> Mitigation: strict schema validation in CI + backwards compatibility test harness",
    "Risk: Cost overruns from unbounded batching -> Mitigation: default per-route throttles + billing alerts",
    "Risk: Entitlement or quota misconfig leads to customer impact -> Mitigation: staged rollout with quota enforcement and explicit billing tests"
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    "Runtime team: batching and KV cache toggles must be available via route config",
    "Console: dashboards and rollout controls implemented and tested",
    "SDK: JS and Python clients with new API surface and streaming primitives",
    "Security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration completion",
    "Legal/Billing: pricing tiers agreed and billing pipeline tested"
  ],
  "stakeholders": [
    "PM: Sofia Patel",
    "Eng (Runtime): Priya Natarajan",
    "Eng (API): Marcus Rivera",
    "Design: Leo Martinez",
    "Security: Hannah Kim",
    "Support: Anika Shah",
    "Sales: Daniel Ortiz"
  ],
  "open_decisions": [
    "Final verb names for streaming endpoints (stream vs SSE vs chunked) \u2014 decision needed by 2025-02-25",
    "Default batching window (20ms vs 40ms) \u2014 leaning 20ms but waiting perf test results",
    "Embeddings batch size max: 8 or 16 \u2014 impact analysis in progress"
  ],
  "links": [
    "Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/hosted-api/acceptance-matrix",
    "OpenAPI: https://api.redwood.ai/specs/hosted-api-2025-03.yaml",
    "Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/design/hosted-api-console-rollout",
    "Load tests: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/hosted-api-canary-2025-02",
    "PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8153"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-02-13 Sofia Patel: Initial draft posted; asked runtime and API leads for input on batching knobs.",
    "2025-02-15 Marcus Rivera: Added definitive API contract section and requested OpenAPI generation from API infra team.",
    "2025-02-17 Priya Natarajan: Raised concern about default caching affinity for chat; proposed 'conversation_token' header to improve KV hit rate.",
    "2025-02-18 Hannah Kim: Security review scheduled for 2025-02-21; noted KMS integration needs test fixture for key rotation",
    "2025-02-20 Design sign-off: Leo Martinez reviewed console flows; requested explicit error states for streaming interruptions"
  ],

    "content": "{\n  \"key\": \"PM-27581\",\n  \"team\": \"product-management\",\n  \"title\": \"Capability-based Staged Launch PRD and Acceptance Matrix for Endpoint Features\",\n  \"status\": \"In Progress\",\n  \"priority\": \"P1\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-10-28\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2026-03-12\",\n  \"creator\": \"Asha Patel\",\n  \"assignee\": \"Priya Shah\",\n  \"project\": \"hosted-endpoints-unification\",\n  \"cycle\": \"Cycle 48\",\n  \"estimate\": \"8\",\n  \"due_date\": \"2026-04-15\",\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"PRD\",\n    \"launch\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"chat\",\n    \"embeddings\",\n    \"rerank\",\n    \"completions\",\n    \"staged-rollout\"\n  ],\n  \"release\": \"hosted-api-2026.04\",\n  \"security_review_required\": \"true\",\n  \"customer_impact\": \"high\",\n  \"dependencies\": [\n    \"ENG-4021\",\n    \"DES-2140\",\n    \"PM-26111\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"This PRD defines a capability-by-capability staged launch for the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: ship a minimal, stable public API surface while enabling rapid iteration on performance and observability. We split launch into three capability gates (Core Completions, Conversational Chat, Embeddings + Rerank) to reduce blast radius and accelerate customer feedback loops. Document covers API contracts, acceptance criteria, rollout schedule, monitoring/SLOs, migration paths and launch checklist.\",\n  \"scope_in_scope\": [\n    \"Core HTTP endpoints for text completions (sync/stream) with consistent parameters across models\",\n    \"Conversational chat endpoint supporting streaming, function/tool calling shim, and token-level usage reporting\",\n    \"Embeddings endpoint supporting multiple vector sizes and L2/cosine normalization paths\",\n    \"Rerank endpoint that accepts candidate lists + query, returns stable scores and ranked order\",\n    \"Server-side defaults for batching and KV cache behavior; runtime-level SLOs applied per-route\",\n    \"Console pages and route-level latency/cost dashboards for each capability\",\n    \"SDK updates (Python + TypeScript) exposing new endpoints and streaming helpers\",\n    \"Canary and phased rollout controls (alpha -> private beta -> GA) with automatic fallback policies\"\n  ],\n  \"out_of_scope\": [\n    \"Dedicated/Dedicated capacity contracts or Dedicated-only features\",\n    \"Private/VPC on-prem packaging for initial GA (will be follow-up)\",\n    \"Full model catalog migration; this PRD assumes model variants are mapped to compatible routes\",\n    \"Large-scale OLAP billing analytics; only per-token and per-route nearline dashboards are required for launch\"\n  ],\n  \"api_contract_changes\": [\n    \"Introduce POST /v1/hosted/completions with payload fields: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, stream (boolean), metadata (opaque map)\",\n    \"Introduce POST /v1/hosted/chat with messages array, optional functions definition, streaming support via SSE/chunked transfer\",\n    \"Embeddings: POST /v1/hosted/embeddings supports model and input array; returns id, vector, model, normalized_vector (when requested)\",\n    \"Rerank: POST /v1/hosted/rerank accepts query and candidates[]; response must include score (float 0-1) and stable_rank_id for deterministic tie-breaks\",\n    \"Backward compatibility: existing client parameters must map to new route equivalents; 30-day deprecation window for legacy fields\",\n    \"Rate limiting: per-route quota keys with soft 95th-percentile limits and hard global caps to prevent noisy neighbors\"\n  ],\n  \"acceptance_criteria\": [\n    \"Completions: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts (<64 tokens) on default model during GA traffic in hosted region\",\n    \"Completions: streaming responses maintain <150ms first-byte latency for streaming-enabled responses\",\n    \"Chat: function calling flow returns structured function JSON in expected schema and preserves conversation-level token accounting\",\n    \"Embeddings: end-to-end roundtrip for 1k inputs (avg 256 tokens) completes within target throughput baseline and embedding vectors match reference precision (within 1.5% L2 error) for quantized models\",\n    \"Rerank: Spearman correlation with reference reranker >= 0.88 across internal eval set; stable ranking behavior across identical inputs\",\n    \"SLOs: error rate < 0.1% (5xx) sustained during canary -> GA transition; automated fallback to last-stable model on detected regressions\",\n    \"Monitoring: dashboards show token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, and per-model throughput; alert on 95th-latency degradation and cost-per-token delta > 15%\",\n    \"Security: KMS encrypted customer metadata at rest; audit log entries present for all admin actions; security review signoff recorded\",\n    \"Docs: API reference, SDK examples, migration guide, and sample prompts published before GA\",\n    \"SDKs: Python and TypeScript clients have parity for the new endpoints and streaming patterns and pass integration tests\"\n  ],\n  \"rollout_plan\": [\n    \"Phase 0 (Internal Alpha): Enable endpoints behind feature flags for Redwood-internal teams and SRE; run synthetic load and collect traces (2 weeks)\",\n    \"Phase 1 (Partner Beta): Invite 3-5 trusted partners with production-like traffic; enable canary autoscaling and rollback automation (4 weeks)\",\n    \"Phase 2 (Public Beta): Open to self-serve signups with limited quota; enable public dashboards and usage analytics; monitor for regressions (6 weeks)\",\n    \"Phase 3 (GA): Lift quotas, publish pricing, and enable region expansion; communicate deprecation timeline for legacy endpoints (2 weeks)\",\n    \"Rollback policy: automated circuit breaker triggers rollback to pre-rollout model variant and notifies on-call; manual override with documented playbook\"\n  ],\n  \"launch_checklist\": [\n    \"Product: Final PRD approved by PM and Eng leads\",\n    \"Engineering: API endpoints implemented and integration tests passing in staging\",\n    \"Engineering: Canary deployment automation + rollback hooks validated\",\n    \"Design: Console UX for route dashboards and per-token breakdowns reviewed and signed off\",\n    \"Security: KMS/HSM integration validated and security review completed\",\n    \"Docs: Public API reference, migration guide, examples, and changelog entries published\",\n    \"SDKs: Python and TypeScript packages released with migration notes\",\n    \"SRE/Observability: Dashboards and alerts deployed to production monitoring stack\",\n    \"Billing: Pricing rules and quota enforcement configured in billing service; cost ETA validated\",\n    \"Sales & CS: Launch kit + FAQ + known limitations doc shared with GTM\",\n    \"Support: Runbook for common issues and escalation path published\",\n    \"Regression Tests: Perf regression set executed across top 5 latency-sensitive models\",\n    \"Legal/Compliance: Data processing addendum templates ready for customers requiring DPAs\"\n  ],\n  \"monitoring_and_slo\": [\n    \"Per-route latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets defined per capability (e.g., completions p95 <250ms)\",\n    \"Token-accurate billing telemetry exposed in console and exported to BigQuery daily\",\n    \"Error budget policy for GA rollouts tied to canary windows with automated pauses if budget depletion > 20%\",\n    \"Anomaly detection: automated drift detection on embedding distributions and sampling-based quality checks\",\n    \"On-call runbook: triage steps for high latency, increased error rate, and cost spikes\"\n  ],\n  \"migration_and_deprecation_plan\": [\n    \"30-day deprecation for legacy fields with automatic header-based opt-in to new behavior\",\n    \"Migration guide with code snippets for common client  \"Evan Brooks - Engineering Lead (Runtime)\",\n    \"Marta Ivanova - SRE\",\n    \"Luca Hern\\u00e1ndez - SDK Lead\",\n    \"Priya Shah - Product Manager (Assignee)\",\n    \"Nina Zhang - Requesting alignment on API surface for streaming vs chunked transfer. document.title: Capability-based Staged Launch PRD and Acceptance Matrix for Endpoint Features
document.content:
{
  "key": "PM-27581",
  "team": "product-management",
  "title": "Capability-based Staged Launch PRD and Acceptance Matrix for Endpoint Features",
  "status": "In Progress",
  "priority": "P1",
  "created_at": "2025-10-28",
  "updated_at": "2026-03-12",
  "creator": "Asha Patel",
  "assignee": "Priya Shah",
  "project": "hosted-endpoints-unification",
  "cycle": "Cycle 48",
  "estimate": "8",
  "due_date": "2026-04-15",
  "labels": [
    "PRD",
    "launch",
    "hosted-api",
    "chat",
    "embeddings",
    "rerank",
    "completions",
    "staged-rollout"
  ],
  "release": "hosted-api-2026.04",
  "security_review_required": "true",
  "customer_impact": "high",
  "dependencies": [
    "ENG-4021",
    "DES-2140",
    "PM-26111"
  ],
  "description": "This PRD defines a capability-by-capability staged launch for the hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Goal: ship a minimal, stable public API surface while enabling rapid iteration on performance and observability. We split launch into three capability gates (Core Completions, Conversational Chat, Embeddings + Rerank) to reduce blast radius and accelerate customer feedback loops. Document covers API contracts, acceptance criteria, rollout schedule, monitoring/SLOs, migration paths and launch checklist.",
  "scope_in_scope": [
    "Core HTTP endpoints for text completions (sync/stream) with consistent parameters across models",
    "Conversational chat endpoint supporting streaming, function/tool calling shim, and token-level usage reporting",
    "Embeddings endpoint supporting multiple vector sizes and L2/cosine normalization paths",
    "Rerank endpoint that accepts candidate lists + query, returns stable scores and ranked order",
    "Server-side defaults for batching and KV cache behavior; runtime-level SLOs applied per-route",
    "Console pages and route-level latency/cost dashboards for each capability",
    "SDK updates (Python + TypeScript) exposing new endpoints and streaming helpers",
    "Canary and phased rollout controls (alpha -> private beta -> GA) with automatic fallback policies"
  ],
  "out_of_scope": [
    "Dedicated/Dedicated capacity contracts or Dedicated-only features",
    "Private/VPC on-prem packaging for initial GA (will be follow-up)",
    "Full model catalog migration; this PRD assumes model variants are mapped to compatible routes",
    "Large-scale OLAP billing analytics; only per-token and per-route nearline dashboards are required for launch"
  ],
  "api_contract_changes": [
    "Introduce POST /v1/hosted/completions with payload fields: model, prompt, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, stream (boolean), metadata (opaque map)",
    "Introduce POST /v1/hosted/chat with messages array, optional functions definition, streaming support via SSE/chunked transfer",
    "Embeddings: POST /v1/hosted/embeddings supports model and input array; returns id, vector, model, normalized_vector (when requested)",
    "Rerank: POST /v1/hosted/rerank accepts query and candidates[]; response must include score (float 0-1) and stable_rank_id for deterministic tie-breaks",
    "Backward compatibility: existing client parameters must map to new route equivalents; 30-day deprecation window for legacy fields",
    "Rate limiting: per-route quota keys with soft 95th-percentile limits and hard global caps to prevent noisy neighbors"
  ],
  "acceptance_criteria": [
    "Completions: 95th percentile latency < 250ms for short prompts (<64 tokens) on default model during GA traffic in hosted region",
    "Completions: streaming responses maintain <150ms first-byte latency for streaming-enabled responses",
    "Chat: function calling flow returns structured function JSON in expected schema and preserves conversation-level token accounting",
    "Embeddings: end-to-end roundtrip for 1k inputs (avg 256 tokens) completes within target throughput baseline and embedding vectors match reference precision (within 1.5% L2 error) for quantized models",
    "Rerank: Spearman correlation with reference reranker >= 0.88 across internal eval set; stable ranking behavior across identical inputs",
    "SLOs: error rate < 0.1% (5xx) sustained during canary -> GA transition; automated fallback to last-stable model on detected regressions",
    "Monitoring: dashboards show token-level cost, per-route latency percentiles, and per-model throughput; alert on 95th-latency degradation and cost-per-token delta > 15%",
    "Security: KMS encrypted customer metadata at rest; audit log entries present for all admin actions; security review signoff recorded",
    "Docs: API reference, SDK examples, migration guide, and sample prompts published before GA",
    "SDKs: Python and TypeScript clients have parity for the new endpoints and streaming patterns and pass integration tests"
  ],
  "rollout_plan": [
    "Phase 0 (Internal Alpha): Enable endpoints behind feature flags for Redwood-internal teams and SRE; run synthetic load and collect traces (2 weeks)",
    "Phase 1 (Partner Beta): Invite 3-5 trusted partners with production-like traffic; enable canary autoscaling and rollback automation (4 weeks)",
    "Phase 2 (Public Beta): Open to self-serve signups with limited quota; enable public dashboards and usage analytics; monitor for regressions (6 weeks)",
    "Phase 3 (GA): Lift quotas, publish pricing, and enable region expansion; communicate deprecation timeline for legacy endpoints (2 weeks)",
    "Rollback policy: automated circuit breaker triggers rollback to pre-rollout model variant and notifies on-call; manual override with documented playbook"
  ],
  "launch_checklist": [
    "Product: Final PRD approved by PM and Eng leads",
    "Engineering: API endpoints implemented and integration tests passing in staging",
    "Engineering: Canary deployment automation + rollback hooks validated",
    "Design: Console UX for route dashboards and per-token breakdowns reviewed and signed off",
    "Security: KMS/HSM integration validated and security review completed",
    "Docs: Public API reference, migration guide, examples, and changelog entries published",
    "SDKs: Python and TypeScript packages released with migration notes",
    "SRE/Observability: Dashboards and alerts deployed to production monitoring stack",
    "Billing: Pricing rules and quota enforcement configured in billing service; cost ETA validated",
    "Sales & CS: Launch kit + FAQ + known limitations doc shared with GTM",
    "Support: Runbook for common issues and escalation path published",
    "Regression Tests: Perf regression set executed across top 5 latency-sensitive models",
    "Legal/Compliance: Data processing addendum templates ready for customers requiring DPAs"
  ],
  "monitoring_and_slo": [
    "Per-route latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 targets defined per capability (e.g., completions p95 <250ms)",
    "Token-accurate billing telemetry exposed in console and exported to BigQuery daily",
    "Error budget policy for GA rollouts tied to canary windows with automated pauses if budget depletion > 20%",
    "Anomaly detection: automated drift detection on embedding distributions and sampling-based quality checks",
    "On-call runbook: triage steps for high latency, increased error rate, and cost spikes"
  ],
  "migration_and_deprecation_plan": [
    "30-day deprecation for legacy fields with automatic header-based opt-in to new behavior",
    "Migration guide with code snippets for common client libraries and a small conversion script in repo",
    "A/B compatibility shim for 60 days to allow gradual client rollout",
    "Telemetry to detect remaining legacy usage and automated emails to high-volume customers still using legacy parameters"
  ],
  "docs_and_sdk_tasks": [
    "Write API reference pages for each endpoint with full request/response examples",
    "Add streaming example notebooks (Python + Node) demonstrating partial response handling",
    "Publish migration guide with code diffs and example prompts",
    "Release SDK patches and coordinate with package maintainers for staged rollout",
    "Update quickstarts and sample apps to use new host-prefixed endpoints"
  ],
  "metrics": [
    "Adoption: number of unique API keys calling new endpoints per week",
    "Latency: p95 response time per endpoint",
    "Cost: average cost-per-1k-tokens per route and delta vs baseline",
    "Quality: rerank Spearman correlation and embeddings retrieval recall@10 on internal evals",
    "Reliability: 5xx rate and successful rollback events during rollout"
  ],
  "risks_and_mitigation": [
    "Risk: Streaming semantics differ across SDKs -> Mitigation: ship streaming compatibility layer and additional integration tests",
    "Risk: Embedding normalization differences cause customer model drift -> Mitigation: expose both raw and normalized vectors and document recommended pipeline",
    "Risk: Rerank instability across quantized models -> Mitigation: enforce deterministic tie-breaker and run cross-model regression tests",
    "Risk: Cost spikes as batching rules change -> Mitigation: provide early-warning alerts and opt-out flag per-customer",
    "Risk: Delayed security review -> Mitigation: escalate to Security leadership and block GA until signoff"
  ],
  "links": [
    "https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/Hosted+Endpoint+Capability+PRD",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/hosted-api/pull/1284",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/402",
    "https://analytics.redwood.com/dashboards/hosted-endpoints-summary",
    "https://docs.redwood.com/guides/migration-to-hosted-endpoints"
  ],
  "stakeholders": [
    "Asha Patel - PM",
    "Evan Brooks - Engineering Lead (Runtime)",
    "Marta Ivanova - SRE",
    "Luca Hern\u00e1ndez - SDK Lead",
    "Priya Shah - Product Manager (Assignee)",
    "Nina Zhang - Security"
  ],
  "comments": [
    "2025-11-03 | Asha Patel: Initial draft circulated to Eng and Design. Requesting alignment on API surface for streaming vs chunked transfer. Action: Eng to confirm whether SSE or HTTP chunking is preferred by 2025-11-10.",
    "2025-11-12 | Evan Brooks: Engineering prefers chunked transfer for current runtime due to easier backpressure handling. Will provide a small compatibility shim for SSE consumers. Estimated effort: 3 points.",
    "2025-12-08 | Luca Hern\u00e1ndez: SDK streaming PR opened (gh#402). Note: Node streaming behavior differs for large payloads; adding extra test coverage. Beta partners flagged a smaller default chunk size to avoid client OOMs.",
    "2026-01-22 | Marta Ivanova: Canary run with internal traffic showed p95 spike at 03:15 UTC due to a misconfigured autoscaler. Mitigation: tighten scale-down threshold and add a warmup buffer. Follow-up: ENG-4239 created.",
    "2026-02-14 | Priya Shah: Security signoff received for KMS integration; pending final documentation of audit log retention policy (target 2026-02-21).",
    "2026-03-10 | Asha Patel: Decision log: Split GA into capability gates (completions -> chat -> embeddings+rerank) to reduce blast radius. Updated acceptance criteria to include rerank correlation threshold."
  ],
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "scope_in_scope",
    "out_of_scope",
    "api_contract_changes",
    "acceptance_criteria",
    "rollout_plan",
    "launch_checklist",
    "monitoring_and_slo",
    "migration_and_deprecation_plan",
    "docs_and_sdk_tasks",
    "metrics",
    "risks_and_mitigation",
    "comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_d9389a58eb4047e8ba2deeac90223fb6"
}

# Hosted API Launch Readiness Decision

**Decision owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Working recommendation:** Pending cross-functional evidence  
**Launch model:** Capability-gated; no date asserted

## Proposed capability and scope

Redwood proposes a unified Hosted API surface for completions, chat, embeddings, and server-side rerank, with backward-compatible aliases, versioned contracts, REST/OpenAPI documentation, JS/Python SDK support, per-route quotas, and Console cost/latency telemetry. The staged capability order is **completions → chat → embeddings + rerank** to reduce blast radius. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity are outside this decision.

## Product gates currently satisfied

- Product scope and capability ordering are defined.
- Required endpoint behaviors and backward-compatibility expectations are documented.
- Measurable functional, performance, telemetry, security, documentation, and support acceptance categories exist.
- Rollout is defined as internal staging, canary, regional expansion, then GA, with explicit error-, latency-, correctness-, and cost-based hold/rollback thresholds.
- Design has reviewed Console flows; the acceptance design requires per-route latency/cost visibility and trace links.

These are **definition gates**, not evidence that production acceptance tests have passed.

## Unresolved delivery items

| Item | Status / evidence | Owner | Launch effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| OpenAPI and example payloads | Todo | Docs team | Blocks public surface |
| JS/Python SDK RC1 with streaming and rerank helpers | In progress | SDK team / ENG-39012; Luca Hernandez | Blocks capability clients |
| Staging performance run and benchmark | In progress | Performance Engineering | Blocks SLO acceptance |
| Streaming parity / Node large-payload coverage and SSE compatibility shim | In progress | Evan Brooks / Luca Hernandez | Blocks chat gate |

| Audit-log retention documentation | Pending in current product record | Security / Nina Zhang | Blocks final security evidence |
| Customer communications and migration guidance | Todo | Growth / PM | Blocks external rollout |

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_51a1f00ca59746048c0c3ebba28c4862",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json",
    "title": "Hosted API Tail Latency SLO Guardrails (Mixed-Workload Scheduler Canary)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Hosted API Tail Latency SLO Guardrails (Mixed-Workload Scheduler Canary)\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-sre\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Bello\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-12-04\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Lena Fischer\",\n    \"Paula Mendes\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"sre\",\n    \"slo\",\n    \"error-budget\",\n    \"tail-latency\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"scheduler\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/mixed-workload-scheduler-rollout-runbook\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/scheduler-class-metrics-dashboard-spec\",\n    \"confluence://eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/mixed-workload-scheduler-prototype-design\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"content\": \"h1. Purpose\\nThis page defines SRE guardrails for enabling the *mixed-workload scheduler prototype* in the *Hosted API* environment. The goal is to reduce user-visible tail latency under mixed short/long prompt distributions while keeping reliability and unit economics within acceptable bounds.\\n\\nThis document is specifically for *canary and ramp phases* (feature-flagged). For steady-state SLO definitions and reporting, see the canonical Hosted API SLO pages.\\n\\nh1. Scope\\n*In scope*\\n* Hosted API traffic served by Redwood inference pools (regional) where the scheduler prototype is enabled behind a feature flag.\\n* Tail latency guardrails: p95/p99 drift, rollback triggers, and error-budget considerations.\\n* Regions/pools: initial canary region(s) and subsequent ramps.\\n\\n*Out of scope*\\n* Dedicated and Private environments (separate guardrails; may reuse thresholds with different blast radius assumptions).\\n* Full QoS productization or customer-tier fairness policies.\\n\\nh1. Definitions\\n* *p95/p99 latency:* percentile latency over a defined aggregation window.\\n* *TTFT:* time-to-first-token (streaming).\\n* *E2E latency:* request start to completion (non-streaming or full-stream completion time).\\n* *Canary pool:* subset of capacity (e.g., 1\\u20135% of traffic or a small set of GPU pools) with feature enabled.\\n* *Baseline:* comparable period immediately prior to enabling the canary (same day-of-week/time-of-day) or a matched control pool (preferred).\\n* *Drift:* (canary metric - baseline metric) / baseline metric.\\n\\nh1. Metrics to monitor (minimum set)\\nThe canary is considered safe only if ALL of the following remain within thresholds.\\n\\nh2. User-visible tail latency\\nPrimary user-visible signals (evaluate by route/model where possible):\\n* Chat/completions *TTFT p95* and *TTFT p99*\\n* Chat/completions *E2E p95* and *E2E p99*\\n* Non-streaming generation *E2E p95/p99* (if applicable for specific endpoints)\\n\\nRecommended dimensions:\\n* region, pool, model, route (chat/completions), request_type (streaming/non-streaming)\\n\\nh2. Queueing and scheduler health (guardrail signals)\\nThese are leading indicators and should be watched during ramp windows:\\n* Queue time p95 and p99 (overall and by scheduler class)\\n* Per-class queue depth (short vs long)\\n* Starvation counters / aging-trigger counters\\n* Dispatch share by class (fraction of iterations serviced)\\n* Prefill latency p95/p99 and decode iteration latency p95/p99\\n\\nh2. Reliability and correctness\\n* HTTP 5xx rate (overall, by route)\\n* Timeout rate / client disconnect rate\\n* Retry rate (if applicable)\\n* GPU OOM / kernel errors / runtime crash loops\\n\\nh2. Unit economics (secondary guardrail)\\nThis is not a rollback trigger unless extreme, but should be tracked:\\n* Tokens/sec per GPU (or equivalent throughput)\\n* Cost-per-1K-tokens proxy metrics (internal)\\n\\nh1. Guardrail thresholds (Hosted API canary)\\nThresholds below assume the canary is *feature-flagged and reversible within minutes*.\\n\\nh2. Evaluation windows\\nUse all three views to avoid missing brief spikes or slow burns:\\n1) *5-minute* window (fast detection of immediate regressions)\\n2) *30-minute* window (stability during sustained load)\\n3) *2-hour* window (captures diurnal patterns during ramp)\\n\\nBaseline selection:\\n* Preferred: control pool in same region with feature disabled.\\n* Acceptable: immediate pre-change baseline (same day) if control is not available.\\n\\nh2. Allowed drift thresholds (tail latency)\\nThe canary must remain within the following *relative drift* limits compared to baseline/control.\\n\\n|| Metric || 5-min allowed drift || 30-min allowed drift || 2-hr allowed drift || Notes ||\\n| TTFT p95 | +5% | +3% | +2% | TTFT is most user-visible for chat; treat as highest priority. |\\n| TTFT p99 | +10% | +7% | +5% | p99 is noisy; sustained drift is the key. |\\n| E2E p95 | +7% | +5% | +3% | Applies to streaming completion time and non-streaming E2E. |\\n| E2E p99 | +12% | +10% | +7% | Use additional sanity check by route/model to isolate hotspots. |\\n\\nAbsolute floor checks (to avoid \\u201csmall relative drift\\u201d hiding large absolute impact):\\n* If TTFT p95 increases by *> +75ms* for a major route (top 3 by QPS) in a region, treat as a guardrail breach even if relative drift is within % thresholds.\\n* If TTFT p99 increases by *> +200ms* sustained over 30 minutes, treat as a guardrail breach.\\n\\nh2. SLO error-budget considerations\\nWe do not \\u201cspend\\u201d tail-latency error budget casually during canary. Guardrails tie directly to error-budget burn to prevent a slow rollout from consuming monthly budget.\\n\\nPolicy:\\n* If the canary causes an estimated *tail-latency SLO burn rate > 2x* the normal regional burn rate over a *30-minute* window, pause ramp.\\n* If the canary causes an estimated *tail-latency SLO burn rate > 5x* over any *15-minute* window, rollback immediately.\\n* If a region is already in an *error budget watch* state (burn > 1x over last 6 hours), do not expand canary in that region; use a healthier region or defer.\\n\\nNotes:\\n* Tail latency SLO burn is computed using the existing SLO pipeline; if per-route/per-model SLO is unavailable, use the closest aggregated service-level SLO but require additional drill-down by route/model for confirmation.\\n\\nh1. Rollback triggers\\nRollback means: disable the scheduler feature flag in the impacted pool(s) and return to baseline scheduling policy. If rollback is not immediately possible due to config propagation issues, apply the \\u201csafe mode\\u201d parameter profile (see below) and page runtime owner.\\n\\nh2. Immediate rollback (page SRE on-call + runtime owner)\\nTrigger any of the following:\\n* TTFT p95 drift > +10% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows in the canary pool.\\n* TTFT p99 drift > +15% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows.\\n* E2E p95 drift > +12% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows.\\n* Any sustained *5xx* increase > +0.2% absolute over 10 minutes attributable to the canary pool.\\n* Any sign of scheduler starvation defect:\\n  * Starvation counter increasing continuously for > 10 minutes, or\\n  * Long-class queue depth grows monotonically for > 15 minutes while short-class remains stable, indicating long-class not making progress.\\n* GPU/runtime stability breach:\\n  * Crash loop, repeated kernel errors, OOM spikes correlated to canary enablement.\\n\\nh2. Pause ramp (hold at current %) and investigate\\nTrigger any of the following:\\n* TTFT p95 drift > +5% sustained over 30 minutes.\\n* Tail-latency SLO burn rate > 2x sustained over 30 minutes.\\n* Queue time p95 drift > +20% sustained over 30 minutes.\\n* Throughput regression > 5% (tokens/sec per GPU) sustained over 2 hours with no corresponding tail-latency win.\\n\\nh2. Proceed criteria (required to ramp up)\\nAll must be true:\\n* No immediate rollback triggers observed in last 60 minutes.\\n* TTFT p95 drift <= +3% over last 30 minutes.\\n* TTFT p99 drift <= +7% over last 30 minutes.\\n* Starvation counter stable (no sustained increases) and long-class is making measurable progress.\\n* SLO burn rate not elevated (> 1.5x) over last 2 hours.\\n\\nh1. Region and pool selection guardrails\\nTo limit blast radius and reduce confounding:\\n* Start in *one region* with historically stable tail latency and sufficient headroom.\\n* Prefer pools with *mixed workload* signature (observed queue-time variability) to validate improvement, but avoid regions currently handling incident response or capacity constraints.\\n* Avoid ramping during known traffic peaks unless explicitly planned and staffed.\\n\\nSuggested ramp sequence (Hosted API):\\n1) 1% traffic to canary pool (or smallest viable pool) for 2 hours\\n2) 5% for 4 hours\\n3) 10% for 24 hours (includes at least one peak period)\\n4) 25% for 24\\u201348 hours\\n5) 50% and then 100% after approval checkpoint\\n\\nApproval checkpoints:\\n* 10% -> 25% requires SRE + Serving Runtime sign-off.\\n* 25% -> 50% requires SRE sponsor sign-off.\\n* 50% -> 100% requires SRE sponsor + product stakeholder acknowledgement (Hosted API).\\n\\nh1. Safe mode parameter profile (if rollback is delayed)\\nIf the feature flag cannot be disabled quickly, apply a conservative profile to reduce tail risk:\\n* Reduce short/long skew (increase long share) to prevent starvation.\\n* Enable/strengthen aging (faster promotion of long requests).\\n* Tighten per-iteration token budget caps to limit long-prefill dominance.\\n\\nExact config keys differ by runtime version; reference the rollout runbook for the current knobs and validated safe bounds.\\n\\nh1. Operational procedure during canary\\nh2. Pre-flight checklist (before enabling)\\n1) Confirm dashboards are live for the target region/pool.\\n2) Confirm control pool exists (feature OFF) and is comparable.\\n3) Confirm on-call coverage:\\n   * SRE on-call aware\\n   * Serving Runtime on-call aware\\n   * Release coordinator assigned for the ramp window\\n4) Confirm rollback mechanism:\\n   * Feature flag path validated (dry-run in staging if available)\\n   * Config propagation time understood (< 5 minutes target)\\n\\nh2. During enablement (first 30 minutes)\\n1) Watch TTFT p95/p99 and queue time p95/p99 at 1\\u20135 minute resolution.\\n2) Watch starvation counters and per-class queue depth.\\n3) If a breach occurs, rollback immediately and annotate the timeline.\\n\\nh2. Post-enable monitoring (next 2\\u201324 hours)\\n1) Check 30-min and 2-hr windows against drift thresholds.\\n2) Slice by top routes/models to catch localized regressions.\\n3) Confirm tail-latency improvement under mixed workloads does not hide regressions under homogeneous traffic.\\n\\nh1. Alerting guidance (canary-specific)\\nDuring the canary window, enable temporary alerts scoped to the canary pool:\\n* TTFT p95 drift alert: > +5% for 15 minutes\\n* TTFT p99 drift alert: > +10% for 15 minutes\\n* Queue time p95 drift alert: > +20% for 15 minutes\\n* Starvation counter rate alert: increasing for 10 minutes\\n* 5xx absolute increase alert: > +0.2% for 10 minutes\\n\\nRouting:\\n* Page SRE on-call for immediate rollback triggers.\\n* Notify #eng-runtime and #eng-sre for pause-ramp triggers.\\n\\nh1. Logging and incident hygiene\\n* Every enable/disable action must include:\\n  * timestamp\\n  * region/pool\\n  * feature flag state\\n  * parameter profile (if changed)\\n  * reason (ramp step / rollback)\\n* For any rollback:\\n  * create an incident ticket if user impact exceeded SLO burn thresholds or if rollback was due to correctness/stability risk\\n  * include dashboard links and the exact guardrail breach(s)\\n\\nh1. Ownership and escalation\\n* Primary owner: *SRE* (tail latency SLO compliance)\\n* Runtime owner: *Serving Runtime Scheduling* (feature behavior and parameter tuning)\\n\\nEscalation path:\\n1) SRE on-call (rollback authority)\\n2) Serving Runtime on-call (root-cause and mitigation)\\n3) SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher) for ramp decisions above 10%\\n4) Executive sponsor (Mateo Alvarez) if the canary blocks a committed release or impacts enterprise commitments\\n\\nh1. Change log\\n* 2025-12-04: Initial guardrails published for Hosted API canary (v0).\\n* 2026-01-12: Added absolute TTFT floor checks and clarified burn-rate gating.\\n* 2026-02-10: Updated proceed criteria and added safe mode guidance for delayed rollback scenarios.\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_51a1f00ca59746048c0c3ebba28c4862\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API Tail Latency SLO Guardrails (Mixed-Workload Scheduler Canary)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-sre\n\nabsolute floor checks ( to avoid “ small relative drift ” hiding large absolute impact ) : * if ttft p95 increases by * > + 75ms * for a major route ( top 3 by qps ) in a region, treat as a guardrail breach even if relative drift is within % thresholds. * if ttft p99 increases by * > + 200ms * sustained over 30 minutes, treat as a guardrail breach. h2. slo error - budget considerations we do not “ spend ” tail - latency error budget casually during canary. guardrails tie directly to error - budget burn to prevent a slow rollout from consuming monthly budget.",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API Tail Latency SLO Guardrails (Mixed-Workload Scheduler Canary)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-sre\n\nduring canary. guardrails tie directly to error - budget burn to prevent a slow rollout from consuming monthly budget. policy : * if the canary causes an estimated * tail - latency slo burn rate > 2x * the normal regional burn rate over a * 30 - minute * window, pause ramp. * if the canary causes an estimated * tail - latency slo burn rate > 5x * over any * 15 - minute * window, rollback immediately. * if a region is already in an * error budget watch * state ( burn > 1x over last 6 hours ), do not expand canary in that region ; use a healthier region or defer.",

{
  "title": "Hosted API Tail Latency SLO Guardrails (Mixed-Workload Scheduler Canary)",
  "space": "eng-sre",
  "author": "Aisha Bello",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-12-04",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Lena Fischer",
    "Paula Mendes"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "sre",
    "slo",
    "error-budget",
    "tail-latency",
    "hosted-api",
    "canary",
    "scheduler"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/mixed-workload-scheduler-rollout-runbook",
    "confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/scheduler-class-metrics-dashboard-spec",
    "confluence://eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/mixed-workload-scheduler-prototype-design",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "content": "h1. Purpose
This page defines SRE guardrails for enabling the *mixed-workload scheduler prototype* in the *Hosted API* environment. The goal is to reduce user-visible tail latency under mixed short/long prompt distributions while keeping reliability and unit economics within acceptable bounds.

This document is specifically for *canary and ramp phases* (feature-flagged). For steady-state SLO definitions and reporting, see the canonical Hosted API SLO pages.

h1. Scope
*In scope*
* Hosted API traffic served by Redwood inference pools (regional) where the scheduler prototype is enabled behind a feature flag.
* Tail latency guardrails: p95/p99 drift, rollback triggers, and error-budget considerations.
* Regions/pools: initial canary region(s) and subsequent ramps.

*Out of scope*
* Dedicated and Private environments (separate guardrails; may reuse thresholds with different blast radius assumptions).
* Full QoS productization or customer-tier fairness policies.

h1. Definitions
* *p95/p99 latency:* percentile latency over a defined aggregation window.
* *TTFT:* time-to-first-token (streaming).
* *E2E latency:* request start to completion (non-streaming or full-stream completion time).
* *Canary pool:* subset of capacity (e.g., 1–5% of traffic or a small set of GPU pools) with feature enabled.
* *Baseline:* comparable period immediately prior to enabling the canary (same day-of-week/time-of-day) or a matched control pool (preferred).
* *Drift:* (canary metric - baseline metric) / baseline metric.

h1. Metrics to monitor (minimum set)
The canary is considered safe only if ALL of the following remain within thresholds.

h2. User-visible tail latency
Primary user-visible signals (evaluate by route/model where possible):
* Chat/completions *TTFT p95* and *TTFT p99*
* Chat/completions *E2E p95* and *E2E p99*
* Non-streaming generation *E2E p95/p99* (if applicable for specific endpoints)

Recommended dimensions:
* region, pool, model, route (chat/completions), request_type (streaming/non-streaming)

h2. Queueing and scheduler health (guardrail signals)
These are leading indicators and should be watched during ramp windows:
* Queue time p95 and p99 (overall and by scheduler class)
* Per-class queue depth (short vs long)
* Starvation counters / aging-trigger counters
* Dispatch share by class (fraction of iterations serviced)
* Prefill latency p95/p99 and decode iteration latency p95/p99

h2. Reliability and correctness
* HTTP 5xx rate (overall, by route)
* Timeout rate / client disconnect rate
* Retry rate (if applicable)
* GPU OOM / kernel errors / runtime crash loops

h2. Unit economics (secondary guardrail)
This is not a rollback trigger unless extreme, but should be tracked:
* Tokens/sec per GPU (or equivalent throughput)
* Cost-per-1K-tokens proxy metrics (internal)

h1. Guardrail thresholds (Hosted API canary)
Thresholds below assume the canary is *feature-flagged and reversible within minutes*.

h2. Evaluation windows
Use all three views to avoid missing brief spikes or slow burns:
1) *5-minute* window (fast detection of immediate regressions)
2) *30-minute* window (stability during sustained load)
3) *2-hour* window (captures diurnal patterns during ramp)

Baseline selection:
* Preferred: control pool in same region with feature disabled.
* Acceptable: immediate pre-change baseline (same day) if control is not available.

h2. Allowed drift thresholds (tail latency)
The canary must remain within the following *relative drift* limits compared to baseline/control.

|| Metric || 5-min allowed drift || 30-min allowed drift || 2-hr allowed drift || Notes ||
| TTFT p95 | +5% | +3% | +2% | TTFT is most user-visible for chat; treat as highest priority. |
| TTFT p99 | +10% | +7% | +5% | p99 is noisy; sustained drift is the key. |
| E2E p95 | +7% | +5% | +3% | Applies to streaming completion time and non-streaming E2E. |
| E2E p99 | +12% | +10% | +7% | Use additional sanity check by route/model to isolate hotspots. |

Absolute floor checks (to avoid “small relative drift” hiding large absolute impact):
* If TTFT p95 increases by *> +75ms* for a major route (top 3 by QPS) in a region, treat as a guardrail breach even if relative drift is within % thresholds.
* If TTFT p99 increases by *> +200ms* sustained over 30 minutes, treat as a guardrail breach.

h2. SLO error-budget considerations
We do not “spend” tail-latency error budget casually during canary. Guardrails tie directly to error-budget burn to prevent a slow rollout from consuming monthly budget.

Policy:
* If the canary causes an estimated *tail-latency SLO burn rate > 2x* the normal regional burn rate over a *30-minute* window, pause ramp.
* If the canary causes an estimated *tail-latency SLO burn rate > 5x* over any *15-minute* window, rollback immediately.
* If a region is already in an *error budget watch* state (burn > 1x over last 6 hours), do not expand canary in that region; use a healthier region or defer.

Notes:
* Tail latency SLO burn is computed using the existing SLO pipeline; if per-route/per-model SLO is unavailable, use the closest aggregated service-level SLO but require additional drill-down by route/model for confirmation.

h1. Rollback triggers
Rollback means: disable the scheduler feature flag in the impacted pool(s) and return to baseline scheduling policy. If rollback is not immediately possible due to config propagation issues, apply the “safe mode” parameter profile (see below) and page runtime owner.

h2. Immediate rollback (page SRE on-call + runtime owner)
Trigger any of the following:
* TTFT p95 drift > +10% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows in the canary pool.
* TTFT p99 drift > +15% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows.
* E2E p95 drift > +12% for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows.
* Any sustained *5xx* increase > +0.2% absolute over 10 minutes attributable to the canary pool.
* Any sign of scheduler starvation defect:
  * Starvation counter increasing continuously for > 10 minutes, or
  * Long-class queue depth grows monotonically for > 15 minutes while short-class remains stable, indicating long-class not making progress.
* GPU/runtime stability breach:
  * Crash loop, repeated kernel errors, OOM spikes correlated to canary enablement.

h2. Pause ramp (hold at current %) and investigate
Trigger any of the following:
* TTFT p95 drift > +5% sustained over 30 minutes.
* Tail-latency SLO burn rate > 2x sustained over 30 minutes.
* Queue time p95 drift > +20% sustained over 30 minutes.
* Throughput regression > 5% (tokens/sec per GPU) sustained over 2 hours with no corresponding tail-latency win.

h2. Proceed criteria (required to ramp up)
All must be true:
* No immediate rollback triggers observed in last 60 minutes.
* TTFT p95 drift <= +3% over last 30 minutes.
* TTFT p99 drift <= +7% over last 30 minutes.
* Starvation counter stable (no sustained increases) and long-class is making measurable progress.
* SLO burn rate not elevated (> 1.5x) over last 2 hours.

h1. Region and pool selection guardrails
To limit blast radius and reduce confounding:
* Start in *one region* with historically stable tail latency and sufficient headroom.
* Prefer pools with *mixed workload* signature (observed queue-time variability) to validate improvement, but avoid regions currently handling incident response or capacity constraints.
* Avoid ramping during known traffic peaks unless explicitly planned and staffed.

Suggested ramp sequence (Hosted API):
1) 1% traffic to canary pool (or smallest viable pool) for 2 hours
2) 5% for 4 hours
3) 10% for 24 hours (includes at least one peak period)
4) 25% for 24–48 hours
5) 50% and then 100% after approval checkpoint

Approval checkpoints:
* 10% -> 25% requires SRE + Serving Runtime sign-off.
* 25% -> 50% requires SRE sponsor sign-off.
* 50% -> 100% requires SRE sponsor + product stakeholder acknowledgement (Hosted API).

h1. Safe mode parameter profile (if rollback is delayed)
If the feature flag cannot be disabled quickly, apply a conservative profile to reduce tail risk:
* Reduce short/long skew (increase long share) to prevent starvation.
* Enable/strengthen aging (faster promotion of long requests).
* Tighten per-iteration token budget caps to limit long-prefill dominance.

Exact config keys differ by runtime version; reference the rollout runbook for the current knobs and validated safe bounds.

h1. Operational procedure during canary
h2. Pre-flight checklist (before enabling)
1) Confirm dashboards are live for the target region/pool.
2) Confirm control pool exists (feature OFF) and is comparable.
3) Confirm on-call coverage:
   * SRE on-call aware
   * Serving Runtime on-call aware
   * Release coordinator assigned for the ramp window
4) Confirm rollback mechanism:
   * Feature flag path validated (dry-run in staging if available)
   * Config propagation time understood (< 5 minutes target)

h2. During enablement (first 30 minutes)
1) Watch TTFT p95/p99 and queue time p95/p99 at 1–5 minute resolution.
2) Watch starvation counters and per-class queue depth.
3) If a breach occurs, rollback immediately and annotate the timeline.

h2. Post-enable monitoring (next 2–24 hours)
1) Check 30-min and 2-hr windows against drift thresholds.
2) Slice by top routes/models to catch localized regressions.
3) Confirm tail-latency improvement under mixed workloads does not hide regressions under homogeneous traffic.

h1. Alerting guidance (canary-specific)
During the canary window, enable temporary alerts scoped to the canary pool:
* TTFT p95 drift alert: > +5% for 15 minutes
* TTFT p99 drift alert: > +10% for 15 minutes
* Queue time p95 drift alert: > +20% for 15 minutes
* Starvation counter rate alert: increasing for 10 minutes
* 5xx absolute increase alert: > +0.2% for 10 minutes

Routing:
* Page SRE on-call for immediate rollback triggers.
* Notify #eng-runtime and #eng-sre for pause-ramp triggers.

h1. Logging and incident hygiene
* Every enable/disable action must include:
  * timestamp
  * region/pool
  * feature flag state
  * parameter profile (if changed)
  * reason (ramp step / rollback)
* For any rollback:
  * create an incident ticket if user impact exceeded SLO burn thresholds or if rollback was due to correctness/stability risk
  * include dashboard links and the exact guardrail breach(s)

h1. Ownership and escalation
* Primary owner: *SRE* (tail latency SLO compliance)
* Runtime owner: *Serving Runtime Scheduling* (feature behavior and parameter tuning)

Escalation path:
1) SRE on-call (rollback authority)
2) Serving Runtime on-call (root-cause and mitigation)
3) SRE sponsor (Sean Gallagher) for ramp decisions above 10%
4) Executive sponsor (Mateo Alvarez) if the canary blocks a committed release or impacts enterprise commitments

h1. Change log
* 2025-12-04: Initial guardrails published for Hosted API canary (v0).
* 2026-01-12: Added absolute TTFT floor checks and clarified burn-rate gating.
* 2026-02-10: Updated proceed criteria and added safe mode guidance for delayed rollback scenarios.
