  "body": "Owner: Connor O\u2019Brien (Release)\nLast reviewed: 2025-04-04\nScope: GA enablement for \u201cHosted canary rollout workflow\u201d (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.\n\nThis checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta \u2192 GA) and should be used as the \u201csingle source of truth\u201d for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.\n\n---\n\n1) Release metadata\n\nRelease name: Hosted Canary Rollouts \u2014 GA\nTarget window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon\u2013Thu)\nPrimary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE\nChange classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging\nBlast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.\n\nApprovers (required for GA flip):\n- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)\n- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)\n- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)\n- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)\n- Release: Connor O\u2019Brien\n\nGo/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement\nAgenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan\n\n---\n\n2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)\n\nCode deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):\n[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)\n[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)\n[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)\n[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)\n[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)\n[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)\n[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)\n\nRBAC + permissions:\n[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)\n[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)\n\nDocs readiness:\n[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)\n[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)\n[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)\n\n---\n\n3) Feature flags / config gates\n\nWe are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be \u201cready,\u201d but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.\n\nA) Console UI gating\nFlag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui\nDefault: OFF\nControls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console\nChecklist:\n[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling\n[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)\n[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA\n\nB) Control plane / orchestrator gating\nFlag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator\nDefault: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call\nControls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths\nChecklist:\n[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured\n[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)\n[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)\n\nC) Dataplane enforcement gating\nFlag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting\nDefault: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist\nControls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes\nChecklist:\n[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active\n[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)\n[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)\n\nKill switches (must exist + verified):\n[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)\n[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane\u2026 allowlist mode)\n[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console\u2026 = OFF)\n\nKill switch ownership + execution:\nPrimary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch\nSecondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag\nTertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan\u2019s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode\n\n---\n\n4) Migrations / schema changes\n\nSchema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)\n\nPre-flight:\n[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema\n[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)\n[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists\n\nExecution:\n[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window\n[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold\n[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)\n\nPost-migration validation:\n[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back\n[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)\n[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)\n\nRollback stance for migrations:\n- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).\n- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.\n\n---\n\n5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch\n\nKey signals for release window (must be pinned in the \u201cGA watch\u201d dashboard):\n\nA) Routing correctness\n[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)\n[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)\n[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly\n\nB) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)\n[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)\n[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)\n\nC) System health\n[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints\n[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions\n[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)\n[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)\n\nAlert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):\n- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.\n- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.\n\nConfirm templates exist:\n[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)\n[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)\n\n---\n\n6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration\n\nDefault stop conditions (GA defaults) \u2014 confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:\n[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)\n[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute\n[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline\n[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____\n[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)\n\nSafety checks:\n[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback\n[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)\n[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)\n\nRunbook linkage:\n[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)\n\n---\n\n7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification\n\nGuardrails required for GA (PM-1851):\n[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)\n[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions\n[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback\n[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with \u201chow to fix\u201d guidance\n\nRBAC behaviors:\n[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails\n[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps\n[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs\n\nEdge cases to test (quick checklist):\n[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed \u2192 denied, message displayed\n[ ] Attempt step > max jump \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt rollback without permission \u2192 denied\n[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) \u2192 allowed but stop conditions should not thrash\n\n---\n\n8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)\n\nStage 0 \u2014 Internal dogfood (already in progress)\n[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only\n[ ] Run 1\u20132 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes\n[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer\n\nStage 1 \u2014 Design partner cohort (beta) stability check\n[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker\n[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)\n\nStage 2 \u2014 GA soft launch (allowlist)\nTarget: 10\u201320 tenants over first 48 hours\n[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)\n[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch\n[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies\n\nStage 3 \u2014 GA broad availability\n[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist \u2192 available-by-request \u2192 self-serve (per product decision)\n[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to\n\n---\n\n9) Backout / incident plan\n\nPrinciple: Prefer \u201cstop the bleeding\u201d (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.\n\nBackout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):\n\nLevel 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)\n- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF\n- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split\n- Owner: SRE on-call\n- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5\u201310 minutes; error rate normalizes\n\nLevel 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts\n- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR \u201cwrites disabled\u201d mode\n- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)\n- Owner: Control plane on-call\n\nLevel 3: Hide Console UI entry points\n- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF\n- Effect: customers can\u2019t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds\n- Owner: Release / Console on-call\n\nLevel 4: Full service rollback (last resort)\n- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.\n- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval\n\nIncident triggers (examples):\n- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)\n- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region\n- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations\n- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)\n\nComms plan during incident:\n[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)\n[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet\n[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach\n\n---\n\n10) Verification tests (release-day run)\n\nStaging:\n[ ] Run E2E: create \u2192 start \u2192 1% step \u2192 promote \u2192 pause \u2192 rollback \u2192 confirm baseline restored\n[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves\n[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification\n\nProduction (internal tenant only):\n[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route\n[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)\n[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags\n[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)\n\nPost-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):\n[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline\n[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)\n[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly\n\n---\n\n11) Documentation + support readiness\n\nCustomer docs:\n[ ] \u201cHow to run a canary rollout\u201d updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations\n[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied\n\nInternal docs:\n[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks\n[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags\n\nSupport enablement:\n[ ] Support macro for \u201cHow do I do a percentage rollout?\u201d includes current GA availability rules\n[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %\n\n---\n\n12) Final sign-offs (fill in during go/no-go)\n\nProduct sign-off:\n- Marissa Cole: ____ (date/time)\n- Paula Mendes: ____ (date/time)\n\nEngineering sign-off:\n- Dylan Brooks: ____ (date/time)\n- Ethan Park: ____ (date/time)\n- Mina Haddad: ____ (date/time)\n\nSRE sign-off:\n- Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: ____ (date/time)\n\nSecurity sign-off:\n- Marcus Lin: ____ (date/time)\n\nRelease sign-off:\n- Connor O\u2019Brien: ____ (date/time)\n\nNotes / open items at time of GA:\n- \n- \n\nAppendix: Known GA limitations (keep aligned with PM-1859)\n- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization\n- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA\n- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only\n",

    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28802-policy-engine-guardrails-for-rollout-actions",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28819-telemetry-tagging-rollout-id-and-cohort",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28845-auto-stop-rollback-on-slo-breach",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28877-rollout-activity-log-and-audit-events",
    "GitHub:redwood/pr-28910-add-rollout-cohort-dashboards-and-alert-templates",
    "GitHub:redwood-docs/pr-922-console-hosted-canary-rollouts-ga-docs",
    "GitHub:rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311-rollout-approver-role-and-permissions",
    "Confluence:architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-hosted-rollout-cohorting-and-traffic-splitting",
    "Confluence:oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split",
    "Confluence:security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions",
    "Slack:eng-releases/1740638401-beta-enablement-schedule-and-kill-switch"
  ],
  "body": "Owner: Connor O’Brien (Release)
Last reviewed: 2025-04-04
Scope: GA enablement for “Hosted canary rollout workflow” (percentage-based traffic splitting on Hosted routes) including Console UI, control plane schema, policy guardrails, routing enforcement, telemetry + dashboards, audit logging.

This checklist is written for the GA cut + staged enablement (beta → GA) and should be used as the “single source of truth” for release go/no-go readiness and backout steps.

---

1) Release metadata

Release name: Hosted Canary Rollouts — GA
Target window: Week of 2025-04-07 (Mon–Thu)
Primary on-call coverage required: Eng Platform + SRE
Change classification: Customer-facing feature w/ routing dataplane behavior + new policy paths + audit logging
Blast radius: Per-tenant by feature flag; dataplane change affects routing decisions only when rollout config exists OR flag gates are enabled.

Approvers (required for GA flip):
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & rollouts) + Paula Mendes (policy/telemetry requirements)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Console & tooling), Ethan Park (Control Plane), Mina Haddad (Smart Routing)
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead) or Rafael Mendes (on-call manager)
- Security: Marcus Lin (audit logging/RBAC)
- Release: Connor O’Brien

Go/no-go meeting: 30 mins, day-of enablement
Agenda: open Sev bugs, SLO/alert readiness, runbook readiness, kill switch confirmation, audit log verification, staged rollout plan

---

2) Dependencies (must be merged + deployed prior to GA)

Code deployed to production (verify commit SHAs / deploy IDs in deploy tool):
[ ] Smart Routing traffic splitting primitive deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28741)
[ ] Rollout Orchestrator API + state machine deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28788)
[ ] Policy engine guardrails deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28802)
[ ] Telemetry tagging + aggregation hooks deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28819)
[ ] Auto-stop / rollback wiring deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28845)
[ ] Activity timeline + audit events persistence deployed (GitHub: redwood/pr-28877)
[ ] Cohort dashboards/alert templates available (GitHub: redwood/pr-28910)

RBAC + permissions:
[ ] rollout-approver role + permission mappings deployed (GitHub: rbac-policy-bundle/pr-311)
[ ] Console correctly hides/disables actions when perms missing (create/start/approve/pause/rollback)

Docs readiness:
[ ] Customer docs merged + published (GitHub: redwood-docs/pr-922)
[ ] Internal on-call runbook final (Confluence: runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split)
[ ] Audit event spec final + shared w/ Support/Sales (Confluence: audit-events-rollout-actions)

---

3) Feature flags / config gates

We are using a layered gating approach. GA requires all three layers to be “ready,” but only tenant-level enablement should be expanded.

A) Console UI gating
Flag: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui
Default: OFF
Controls: visibility of Rollouts wizard + timeline views in Console
Checklist:
[ ] Flag exists in prod, is writable by release tooling
[ ] Flag OFF behavior is clean (no dead links, no partial panels)
[ ] Flag ON for internal dogfood tenants only pre-GA

B) Control plane / orchestrator gating
Flag: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator
Default: ON (recommended) or ON for allowlist only depending on risk call
Controls: create/progress/pause/rollback endpoints acceptance; persistence paths
Checklist:
[ ] Validate no background tasks run for tenants without rollouts configured
[ ] Validate idempotency on action endpoints (retry safe)
[ ] Verify orchestrator emits events even when Console UI is off (API-only tenants)

C) Dataplane enforcement gating
Flag: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting
Default: ON (recommended) but only used when a rollout is active OR allowlist
Controls: actual traffic splitting enforcement for Hosted routes
Checklist:
[ ] Verify enforcement is no-op unless rollout config present / active
[ ] Verify deterministic cohorting key per ADR (Confluence ADR: cohorting & traffic splitting)
[ ] Verify region behavior matches GA spec (percent is global per route; region-specific metrics available)

Kill switches (must exist + verified):
[ ] Kill switch 1: disable routing enforcement (routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF)
[ ] Kill switch 2: block new rollouts creation/start for new tenants (control_plane… allowlist mode)
[ ] Kill switch 3: hide Console entry points (console… = OFF)

Kill switch ownership + execution:
Primary: SRE on-call (Sean/Rafael) can flip routing kill switch
Secondary: Release (Connor) can flip Console flag
Tertiary: Control plane on-call (Ethan’s rotation) can switch orchestrator allowlist mode

---

4) Migrations / schema changes

Schema changes (control plane persistence): rollout objects, steps/states, audit/event references (ENG-9131)

Pre-flight:
[ ] Confirm migrations are backward compatible with existing routing policy schema
[ ] Confirm read paths tolerate missing new fields (safe defaults)
[ ] Confirm old Console clients do not crash if new rollout data exists

Execution:
[ ] Migration applied to prod control-plane DB(s) during low-traffic window
[ ] Verify migration completion: no long locks, no replication lag above threshold
[ ] Verify new tables/columns have correct indexes (rollout_id lookups, route_id lookups)

Post-migration validation:
[ ] Create a test rollout in staging and prod-internal tenant; confirm persists and reads back
[ ] Confirm audit event persistence works (rollout_create, rollout_start, step_change, pause, approval, rollback)
[ ] Confirm event retention settings align with security expectations (per audit logging spec)

Rollback stance for migrations:
- Prefer forward-fix: schema additions are not rolled back unless necessary (risk of data loss).
- If hard rollback required: stop all orchestrator writes + disable UI + disable routing enforcement first, then consult DB owner for recovery.

---

5) Monitoring, dashboards, and alerting to watch

Key signals for release window (must be pinned in the “GA watch” dashboard):

A) Routing correctness
[ ] Split adherence: observed canary % vs configured % (global + per-region)
[ ] Cohort assignment stability: % of requests switching cohorts for same user key (should be ~0; watch streaming/retries)
[ ] Retry behavior: ensure retries do not flip cohort unexpectedly

B) Customer-impact SLO signals (baseline vs canary)
[ ] 5xx rate (baseline cohort vs canary cohort)
[ ] timeout rate (baseline vs canary)
[ ] p95 latency (baseline vs canary)
[ ] queue time / admission control signals (if applicable)

C) System health
[ ] Control plane API error rate on rollout endpoints
[ ] Orchestrator background worker lag / stuck transitions
[ ] Metric evaluation timeouts for stop conditions (watch for repeat of beta issue fixed in pr-28895)
[ ] Audit log pipeline: ingestion success rate and export queue depth (if enabled)

Alert policy during GA window (tuning guidance):
- Avoid alert storms: cohort-specific alerts should page only when BOTH: (a) minimum traffic threshold met AND (b) regression above threshold sustained for N minutes.
- Ensure stop-condition triggers do not page twice (auto-pause + alert) unless necessary.

Confirm templates exist:
[ ] Standard cohort comparison panels available (GitHub: observability-pack/pr-184 or redwood/pr-28910)
[ ] Alert templates for auto-stop triggers reviewed by SRE (Sean/Rafael)

---

6) Auto-stop / auto-rollback configuration

Default stop conditions (GA defaults) — confirm they match product decision + SRE sign-off:
[ ] 5xx regression threshold: ____% absolute or ____x relative (fill in final values)
[ ] timeout regression threshold: ____% absolute
[ ] p95 latency regression threshold: +____ ms or +____% over baseline
[ ] Minimum sample size / minimum time window before evaluating: ____
[ ] Soak time minimum between steps: ____ (policy enforced)

Safety checks:
[ ] Confirm auto-stop action is PAUSE by default (vs rollback), unless tenant policy requires rollback
[ ] Confirm rollback is a separate explicit action or only happens after pause + approval (depending on tier)
[ ] Confirm notifications route to correct internal channels for beta/GA (PagerDuty + Slack)

Runbook linkage:
[ ] Stop-condition fired path referenced in runbook (diagnostics, how to resume/rollback)

---

7) Approval gates / policy guardrails verification

Guardrails required for GA (PM-1851):
[ ] Max step size enforced (e.g., cannot jump from 5% to 100% unless policy allows)
[ ] Minimum soak time enforced between step promotions
[ ] Approval required for risky actions (configurable): start rollout, promote above threshold, rollback
[ ] Clear Console error messages on deny with “how to fix” guidance

RBAC behaviors:
[ ] Non-approver cannot approve steps / cannot override guardrails
[ ] Approver role can approve but still cannot exceed hard tenant policy caps
[ ] Audit events record actor, role, IP/user agent (as available), tenant, route, diffs

Edge cases to test (quick checklist):
[ ] Attempt to promote before soak time elapsed → denied, message displayed
[ ] Attempt step > max jump → denied
[ ] Attempt rollback without permission → denied
[ ] Attempt start while missing required metrics (no traffic) → allowed but stop conditions should not thrash

---

8) Release sequencing plan (staged enablement)

Stage 0 — Internal dogfood (already in progress)
[ ] Enable for Redwood internal tenant(s) only
[ ] Run 1–2 real rollouts of non-critical Hosted routes
[ ] Validate audit logs show up in internal audit viewer

Stage 1 — Design partner cohort (beta) stability check
[ ] Confirm no open P0/P1 issues from design partners tracker
[ ] Confirm support escalation path is active (#support-escalations + on-call)

Stage 2 — GA soft launch (allowlist)
Target: 10–20 tenants over first 48 hours
[ ] Enable tenant flag for first batch (coordinate w/ Support + PM)
[ ] Watch dashboards for 1 hour after each batch
[ ] Freeze further enablement if any routing correctness anomalies

Stage 3 — GA broad availability
[ ] Switch default enablement from allowlist → available-by-request → self-serve (per product decision)
[ ] Update support macros and internal enablement how-to

---

9) Backout / incident plan

Principle: Prefer “stop the bleeding” (disable enforcement) over partial rollbacks.

Backout levels (execute in this order for highest safety):

Level 1: Disable routing enforcement (fastest)
- Action: routing.hosted_route_canary_splitting = OFF
- Effect: all traffic goes to baseline routing behavior; rollouts remain visible but do not affect split
- Owner: SRE on-call
- Verification: canary cohort traffic drops to ~0% within 5–10 minutes; error rate normalizes

Level 2: Pause rollouts globally / block new rollouts
- Action: control_plane.hosted_canary_rollouts_orchestrator = allowlist-only OR “writes disabled” mode
- Effect: prevents new rollouts / step promotions; existing rollouts can be paused (manual)
- Owner: Control plane on-call

Level 3: Hide Console UI entry points
- Action: console.hosted_canary_rollouts_ui = OFF
- Effect: customers can’t initiate via Console; reduces load on support while investigation proceeds
- Owner: Release / Console on-call

Level 4: Full service rollback (last resort)
- Roll back orchestrator/routing builds only if a safe previous version is known-good and compatible with new schema.
- Requires: engineering leads approval (Dylan/Ethan/Mina) + SRE approval

Incident triggers (examples):
- Observed split mismatch > 2x expected sustained for > 15 minutes (e.g., config 10%, observed 30%)
- Cross-region inconsistency causing higher-than-expected canary traffic in a single region
- Auto-stop thrashing (pause/resume loops) affecting customer operations
- Audit logging failure for rollout actions (security regression)

Comms plan during incident:
[ ] Start internal incident channel (if Sev2+)
[ ] Notify Support lead (Dev Patel) and create/update customer comms snippet
[ ] For impacted enterprise tenants: direct CSM outreach

---

10) Verification tests (release-day run)

Staging:
[ ] Run E2E: create → start → 1% step → promote → pause → rollback → confirm baseline restored
[ ] Run E2E with approval required: start denied until approver approves
[ ] Force stop-condition breach in staging and verify auto-pause + notification

Production (internal tenant only):
[ ] Create rollout on a low-risk internal Hosted route
[ ] Confirm observed traffic split matches within tolerance (after warmup)
[ ] Confirm dashboards show baseline vs canary metrics with correct tags
[ ] Confirm audit events emitted and visible (and exportable if configured)

Post-enablement spot checks (first external tenants):
[ ] Confirm tenant can see rollout wizard + timeline
[ ] Confirm policy guardrails reflect tenant tier (max step, approvals)
[ ] Confirm support can retrieve rollout_id, state, and recent actions quickly

---

11) Documentation + support readiness

Customer docs:
[ ] “How to run a canary rollout” updated with screenshots and guardrail explanations
[ ] Troubleshooting section includes: split mismatch, auto-paused, stuck step, approval denied

Internal docs:
[ ] How-to enable feature for tenant is accurate and includes sanity checks
[ ] On-call runbook includes: diagnosing wrong split, disabling enforcement, checking cohort tags

Support enablement:
[ ] Support macro for “How do I do a percentage rollout?” includes current GA availability rules
[ ] Escalation template includes required fields: tenant_id, route_id, rollout_id, region, timestamps, expected %

---

12) Final sign-offs (fill in during go/no-go)

Product sign-off:
- Marissa Cole: ____ (date/time)
- Paula Mendes: ____ (date/time)

Engineering sign-off:
- Dylan Brooks: ____ (date/time)
- Ethan Park: ____ (date/time)
- Mina Haddad: ____ (date/time)

SRE sign-off:
- Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes: ____ (date/time)

Security sign-off:
- Marcus Lin: ____ (date/time)

Release sign-off:
- Connor O’Brien: ____ (date/time)

Notes / open items at time of GA:
- 
- 

Appendix: Known GA limitations (keep aligned with PM-1859)
- No multi-armed bandits / dynamic optimization
- Quality gates are optional/manual inputs only; not a blocking automated gate for GA
- Dedicated/Private parity not in GA scope; ensure schema compatibility only

# Hosted API Launch Readiness Decision

**Decision owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Working recommendation:** No production launch until operational blockers close  
**Launch model:** Capability-gated; no date asserted

## Proposed capability and bounded scope

Unified Hosted API for completions, chat, embeddings, and server-side rerank, with backward-compatible aliases, versioned REST/OpenAPI contracts, JS/Python SDKs, per-route quotas, and Console telemetry. Capability order remains **completions → chat → embeddings + rerank**. Dedicated/private deployment bundles and full non-core SDK parity are excluded.

## Reconciled product and operational gates

| Gate | Accepted criterion | Current evidence | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract | Published OpenAPI/examples; compatibility tests green | Required; delivery tracker says OpenAPI/examples todo | Blocked |
| Performance | Production-like benchmark within route SLOs | Benchmark in progress; autoscaler p95 regression follow-up not evidenced closed | Blocked |
| Chat | Streaming order/integrity and long-connection stability; Node coverage | SDK work and extra Node coverage in progress | Blocked |
| Embeddings/rerank | Determinism/fidelity tests green | E2E rerank fidelity suite todo | Blocked |
| Security | Threat model complete; critical/major findings remediated; KMS and retention enforcement verified | KMS signoff reported, but retention documentation remains pending; final launch signoff absent | Blocked |
| Audit/RBAC | Actor, role, tenant, route, diffs and rollout actions logged; permissions enforced | Security event specification published; release verification not recorded | Blocked |
| SRE pre-flight | Live dashboards/control pool; on-call and release coordinator assigned; rollback path validated under 5 minutes | Requirements published; execution evidence absent | Blocked |
| Canary health | No rollback trigger in prior 60m; TTFT p95 ≤ +3% and p99 ≤ +7% over 30m; burn ≤1.5x over 2h | No qualifying run evidenced | Blocked |
| Release | Required deployments, flags, migrations, dashboards, docs, support, and signoffs complete | Release checklist is in review with checkboxes/signoffs unfilled | Blocked |
| Billing | Token accounting and plan enforcement validated | Todo | Blocked |

## Operational gates and rollback policy

- Start in one healthy region with a comparable control pool; use 1% → 5% → 10% → 25% → 50% → 100% progression.
- Pause ramp for TTFT p95 drift above 5% over 30 minutes or tail-latency burn above 2x over 30 minutes.
- Roll back immediately for burn above 5x over 15 minutes; TTFT p95 above +10%, TTFT p99 above +15%, or E2E p95 above +12% for two 5-minute windows; attributable 5xx increase above 0.2% for 10 minutes; starvation, crash loops, kernel errors, or OOM spikes.
- Do not expand a region already in error-budget watch.
- Required checkpoints: SRE + Runtime at 10%→25%; SRE sponsor at 25%→50%; SRE sponsor + Product at 50%→100%.
- Backout order: disable routing enforcement; block/pause rollouts; hide Console entry points; full service rollback only as a last resort. SRE owns the routing kill switch; Control Plane owns orchestrator allowlist/write disable; Release/Console owns UI disable.

## Blockers and owners

1. **Contract/docs:** OpenAPI, examples, quickstarts and migration guidance — Docs / Growth-PM.
2. **SDK/chat:** RC1, SSE compatibility shim, Node large-payload and streaming tests — Luca Hernandez / Evan Brooks.
3. **Performance/capacity:** production-like benchmark and ENG-4239 autoscaler mitigation verification — Performance Eng / Evan Brooks / Marta Ivanova.
4. **Controlled rollout:** per-key targeting, cohort tags, dashboards, alerts, auto-stop/rollback, and rollback rehearsal — Infra / SRE / Observability.
5. **Security:** retention enforcement/documentation, audit-event production verification, RBAC negative tests, final Security approval — Nina Zhang / Marcus Lin.
6. **Billing:** token accounting and plan enforcement E2E — Billing Engineering.
7. **Quality:** randomized E2E conformance, embeddings determinism, rerank fidelity — QA.
8. **Release governance:** deploy IDs/SHAs, migrations, kill switches, on-call coverage, release go/no-go and all named approvals — Connor O’Brien with Product, Engineering, SRE, Security.
9. **Support/customer:** evidence deferred to final pass.

## Evidence

- Linear PM-27581: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-27581-capability-staged-launch-prd-acceptance-matrix.json` (`dsid_d9389a58eb4047e8ba2deeac90223fb6`)

- Linear PM-51555: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-51555-api-family-delivery-specification-chat-embeddings-rerank-launch-rundown.json` (`dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a`)
- Confluence SRE, published: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json` (`dsid_51a1f00ca59746048c0c3ebba28c4862`)
- Confluence Security, published: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json` (`dsid_5f119369627543848ddc03d6805509dd`)
- Google Drive Release Engineering, in review: `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json` (`dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2`)

Path: /artifacts/product/launch-readiness.md

→100%.
- Backout order: disable routing enforcement; block/pause rollouts; hide Console entry points; full service rollback only as a last resort. SRE owns the routing kill switch; Control Plane owns orchestrator allowlist/write disable; Release/Console owns UI disable.

## Blockers and owners

1. **Contract/docs:** OpenAPI, examples, quickstarts and migration guidance — Docs / Growth-PM.
2. **SDK/chat:** RC1, SSE compatibility shim, Node large-payload and streaming tests — Luca Hernandez / Evan Brooks.
3. **Performance/capacity:** production-like benchmark and ENG-4239 autoscaler mitigation verification — Performance Eng / Evan Brooks / Marta Ivanova.
4. **Controlled rollout:** per-key targeting, cohort tags, dashboards, alerts, auto-stop/rollback, and rollback rehearsal — Infra / SRE / Observability.

# Hosted API Launch Readiness Decision

**Decision owner:** Ethan Park, Platform & Console  
**Final recommendation:** **NO-GO for customer launch**  
**Permitted activity:** Internal dogfood and staging validation only; no date asserted

## Decision

Do not launch the planned Hosted API capability to customers yet. Product scope is coherent and the operational criteria are acceptable, but authoritative delivery, release, security, support, and approval records do not show the gates closed. A limited customer allowlist is therefore not yet supported. Internal dogfood may continue behind tenant flags with the routing kill switch validated.

When the blockers below close, the first reviewable customer scope is **completions only**, to a named design-partner allowlist in one healthy region, starting at 1% with a matched control. Chat remains excluded until streaming/Node tests and chunk-size behavior are accepted; embeddings and rerank remain excluded until determinism and rerank-fidelity evidence is green.

## Accepted launch criteria

| Gate | Evidence required to change this decision |
|---|---|
| Contract/docs | Published OpenAPI, examples, JS/Python snippets, migration guide; backward-compatibility suite green |
| Performance/capacity | Production-like benchmark within route SLOs; ENG-4239 autoscaler mitigation verified |
| Security | Threat model complete; no critical/major launch findings; KMS, retention enforcement and audit events verified; Security approval recorded |
| Billing/quotas | Token accounting and plan enforcement pass E2E |
| Canary controls | Per-key/tenant targeting, cohort tags, dashboards, alerts, three kill switches, and forced rollback rehearsal pass |
| SRE pre-flight | Healthy region/control pool, on-call and coordinator assigned, rollback propagation validated under five minutes |
| Canary proceed | No immediate trigger for 60m; TTFT p95 ≤ +3% and p99 ≤ +7% over 30m; SLO burn ≤1.5x over 2h |
| Support | Incident/FAQ runbooks reviewed by L2/L3; macros and escalation template ready; at least two training sessions and sample-ticket evidence recorded |
| Customer readiness | Named design partners accept scope, traffic profile and telemetry; no open P0/P1 partner issues; customer communication approved |
| Governance | Product, Engineering, SRE, Security and Release signoffs recorded at go/no-go |

## Operational thresholds and backout

- Sequence: 1% for 2h → 5% for 4h → 10% for 24h → 25% for 24–48h → 50% → 100%.
- Pause for TTFT p95 drift >5% over 30m or tail-latency burn >2x over 30m.
- Roll back for burn >5x over 15m; TTFT p95 >+10%, TTFT p99 >+15%, or E2E p95 >+12% for two 5m windows; attributable 5xx increase >0.2% for 10m; starvation, crash loop, kernel error, or OOM spike.
- Never expand a region in error-budget watch.
- Approvals: SRE + Runtime at 10%→25%; SRE sponsor at 25%→50%; SRE sponsor + Product at 50%→100%.
- Backout order: disable routing enforcement; block/pause rollout writes; hide Console UI; full binary rollback last.

## Blockers and accountable owners

1. OpenAPI/examples/quickstarts/migration guide — Docs / Growth-PM.
2. JS/Python RC1, SSE shim, Node large-payload and streaming coverage — Luca Hernandez / Evan Brooks.
3. Benchmark and ENG-4239 autoscaler closure — Performance Engineering / Evan Brooks / Marta Ivanova.
4. Targeting, cohort telemetry, alerting, auto-stop and rollback rehearsal — Infrastructure / Observability / SRE.
5. Retention enforcement/documentation, production audit verification, RBAC negative tests, final approval — Nina Zhang / Marcus Lin.
6. Billing and quota E2E — Billing Engineering.
7. Randomized conformance, embeddings determinism, rerank fidelity — QA.
8. Support runbook/FAQ, active escalation, response policy approval, two trainings and sample-ticket proof — Dev Patel / Support leadership / Rafael Mendes.
9. Release deploy evidence, migrations, kill-switch confirmation, staffing and go/no-go record — Connor O’Brien.
10. Cross-functional approvals — Product, Engineering, SRE, Security and Release approvers named in the release checklist.

## Customer and cohort evidence reconciliation

- Beta feedback specifically asks for smaller streaming chunks to avoid client OOMs; this supports holding chat from the first capability gate.
- Customer conversations repeatedly surface retention, audit evidence, SDK reconnect/retry behavior and support SLA as adoption blockers.
- The release model calls for internal dogfood, then a small per-tenant design-partner beta, then a 10–20 tenant soft-launch allowlist with monitoring after each batch; broad availability follows only after those stages.
- Support acceptance requires concrete training and resolved-ticket evidence, not merely a draft runbook. Current support evidence shows preparation and an unapproved pilot response target, while the GA checklist remains in progress.

## Evidence-backed next steps

1. Owners attach closure evidence for blockers 1–7 to the release record.
2. SRE and Release run the staging create→start→promote→pause→rollback test, force a stop-condition breach, and record dashboard/audit evidence.
3. Support completes two recorded trainings, validates macros on sample cases, and gets the launch response policy approved.
4. PM names completions-only design partners and records accepted traffic profiles, region eligibility, communications, and absence of P0/P1 partner issues.
5. Connor O’Brien convenes go/no-go only after evidence is attached; required approvers record decisions.
6. If approved, enable completions for the named allowlist in one healthy region at 1%; do not add chat, embeddings, or rerank by implication.

## Authoritative evidence

- Linear PM-27581 (product scope and capability gates): `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-27581-capability-staged-launch-prd-acceptance-matrix.json` (`dsid_d9389a58eb4047e8ba2deeac90223fb6`)
- Linear PM-51555 (delivery status): `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-51555-api-family-delivery-specification-chat-embeddings-rerank-launch-rundown.json` (`dsid_ada92facaa334d3688c6a8371e0d001a`)
- Linear PM-1859 (support acceptance): `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/product-management/PM-1859-ga-launch-criteria-and-beta-exit-checklist-hosted-canary.json` (`dsid_5444ca17e9664747930ead86571d4804`)
- Confluence SRE (published guardrails): `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/hosted-api-tail-latency-slo-guardrails.json` (`dsid_51a1f00ca59746048c0c3ebba28c4862`)
- Confluence Security (published audit specification): `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-events-rollout-actions.json` (`dsid_5f119369627543848ddc03d6805509dd`)
- Google Drive Release Engineering (in-review GA checklist): `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/hosted-canary-ga-change-management-checklist.json` (`dsid_fa0fb79e2f54457093ad3f831e7ac6a2`)
- Gmail Support/Customer readiness: `/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/laura_bennett/20260311-velocity-pilot-readiness-summary.json` (`dsid_83b3dd4f87f7426f9d9fada0ce98736c`)
- Fireflies Customer Success (streaming/retry documentation need): `/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/customer-success/2026-02-06-enterprise-checkin-sdk-upgrade-and-migration.json` (`dsid_7884f28a415e4daa81556a7a829ec2d0`)
